An independent read-only review of the integrated head found a **blocker**, and it is the same defect class this PR exists to remove — one level up the read chain.

### The finding

#608 closed false-accrual at the **frame** read. The **index** read above it was left open, and on that path the surface states three things that are all false at the same time:

| surface | copy shown on a cold `surface_idx:<ROOT>` 503 | why it is false |
| --- | --- | --- |
| chart | "No surface data yet — accruing. … **Nothing is hidden**." | nothing was read, so nothing is known to be absent |
| replay bar | "this root has none for the selected day" | same claim, restated as fact |
| replay bar | "Refresh unavailable · **retaining stored frames**" | nothing was ever admitted, so nothing is retained |

Mechanism: a failed index admits no stamp, so `asOfStamp` is null, so `SurfacePane`'s no-stamp branch runs and explicitly clears `frameError`. The empty-state ternary then falls through `loading` → `frameError` → `cellAccruing` to `surfaceEmpty`. The repair's own `surfaceUnavailable` string could never be reached on this path.

I reproduced it before accepting it. Discriminating RED on this tree:

```
× reports a cold index transport failure as unavailable, not absence or retention
    Expected: "Surface unavailable"
    Received: "…No surface data yet — accruing.Stamps are written as the session runs —
               until the materializer has painted one there is nothing to shade. Nothing is hidden."
    1 failed | 26 passed
```

- `SurfacePane.tsx` consumes `indexError`. It was **already exposed on the context and simply never read**; `readFailed = frameError || (indexError && indexDate == null)` routes a never-landed index into the existing read-failure state.
- `ReplayBar.tsx` guards the retention wording on frames actually existing, and gives a failed index its own copy rather than borrowing copy that asserts absence.
